hypotheses.reasoning: notif-db's /var/lib/mysql volume filled up. Disk usage warnings escalated 93% (#125) to 96% (#178) to 99% (#213), with WAL/binlog growth of roughly 650-790MB/h. Once the disk was full, InnoDB failed writes to notifications.ibd with 'No space left on device' (#227, #246, #250), and notification-svc inserts failed with error 1114 'The table is full' (#230, #239, #256). Those failures surfaced as 500s at api-gateway (#225, #244, #252 onward), which is the alert symptom. Reads stayed healthy because the fault affects writes only. Gateway 500s and latency are downstream effects. Alternatives considered: the slow audit_log seq scan (#211) may have added WAL pressure but does not explain the write failures; template-svc, redis and notif-worker show no errors; the TLS expiry warning (#65) is unrelated. The cause of the WAL/binlog growth is not visible in the logs.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately free disk space on notif-db: purge or archive old binlogs/WAL files and check for runaway audit_log growth. Then restore write capacity and confirm notification-svc inserts succeed. Afterward, add disk-usage alerting well before 90%, set binlog retention limits, add an index on audit_log(created_at) to replace the seq scan, and review whether the notifications table needs a retention policy.
